about: Flowering window and heat-stress threshold per crop for 'hot days at flowering' in the climate shift block (EP-10, S-10.02). Every value cites a page that was opened on the access date and contains the value or the numbers it is derived from. All entries are verified: false until the owner reviews them; the product labels them 'not yet reviewed'. Windows are 'days after emergence' (published rules of thumb count from emergence); the API converts them to calendar dates with the season record's emergence date, else sowing date plus the typical emergence days of data/crop-phenology.json (itself unverified). A crop without an entry here uses the labelled fallback: days above 35 C in June-August (December-February in the southern hemisphere). Crops left out because no checkable source was found: winter and spring wheat (heat threshold found, no window), soybean (flowering length found, no threshold or start), canola (threshold found, no window), sunflower, cotton, millet, barley.

threshold.note: Both pages name 95 F (= 35 C): 'Temperatures greater than 95 F with low relative humidity will desiccate exposed silks' (Iowa State); 'Heat over 95 F depresses pollen production' (Nebraska). Iowa State adds that high temperature does not severely stress pollination when soil moisture is adequate.
